agonizingly: With extreme anguish or desperate struggles.
agonothete: An officer who presided over the great public games in Greece.
agony: intense feelings of suffering; acute mental or physical pain
agood: In earnest; heartily. I made her weep agood.
agora: An assembly; hence, the place of assembly, especially the market place, in an ancient Greek city.
agoraphobia: a morbid fear of open spaces (as fear of being caught alone in some public place)
agouara: The crab-eating raccoon (Procyon cancrivorus), found in the tropical parts of America.
agouta: A small insectivorous mammal (Solenodon paradox us), allied to the moles, found only in Hayti.

agpaite: Any of various peralkaline igneous rocks, typically nepheline syenite or phonolite.
agra: a city in northern India; former capital of the Mogul empire; site of the Taj Mahal
agrafe: A hook or fastener on clothing.
agraffe: A hook or clasp. The feather of an ostrich, fastened in her turban by an agraffe set with brilliants. Sir W. Scott.
agranulocytic: relating to the blood disorder of agranulocytosis

agrarian: Wild; said of plants growing in the fields.

agree: To correspond in gender, number, case, or person.
agreeable: conforming to your own liking or feelings or nature

agreed: united by being of the same opinion
agreeing: present participle and gerund of agree
agreement: Concord or correspondence of one word with another in gender, number, case, or person.
agrees: third-person singular simple present indicative of agree
agrestic: Pertaining to fields or the country, in opposition to the city; rural; rustic; unpolished; uncouth. Agrestic behavior. " Gregory.
agricola: Roman general who was governor of Britain and extended Roman rule north to the Firth of Forth (-)
agriculturalist: An agriculturist (which is the preferred form.)
agriculturally: In a manner pertaining to agriculture.
agriculture: The art or science of cultivating the ground, including the harvesting of crops, and the rearing and management of live stock; tillage; husbandry; farming.
agriculturist: One engaged or skilled in agriculture; a husbandman. The farmer is always a practitioner, the agriculturist may be a mere theorist. Crabb.
agrimonia: a plant of the genus Agrimonia having spikelike clusters of small yellow flowers
agrimony: A genus of plants of the Rose family.
agrin: In the act of grinning. His visage all agrin. " Tennyson.
agriology: Description or comparative study of the customs of savage or uncivilized tribes.
agrippa: Roman general who commanded the fleet that defeated the forces of Antony and Cleopatra at Actium (- BC)
agrippina: wife who poisoned Claudius after her son Nero was declared heir and who was then put to death by Nero
agrise: To shudder with terror; to tremble with fear. Chaucer.
agrito: A Mexican shrub of species Berberis trifolia.
agrobiology: the study of plant nutrition and growth especially as a way to increase crop yield
agrology: science of soils in relation to crops
agronomic: of or relating to or promoting agronomy
agronomics: The science of the distribution and management of land.
agronomist: One versed in agronomy; a student of agronomy.
agronomy: The management of land; rural economy; agriculture.
agropyron: perennial grasses of temperate and cool regions: wheatgrass; dog grass
agrostemma: a caryophylloid dicot genus including corn cockles
agrostis: A genus of grasses, including species called in common language bent grass. Some of them, as redtop (Agrostis vulgar is), are valuable pasture grasses.
agrostology: That part of botany which treats of the grasses.
aground: On the ground; stranded; a nautical term applied to a ship when its bottom lodges on the ground. Totten.
agrypnia: a vigil before certain feasts (as e.g. Easter)
agua: largest known toad species; native to Central America; valuable destroyer of insect pests
ague: An intermittent fever, attended by alternate cold and hot fits.
agues: third-person singular simple present indicative of ague
agueweed: gentian of eastern North America having clusters of bristly blue flowers
agyrophobia: A fear of crossing the street.
ah: An exclamation, expressive of surprise, pity, complaint, entreaty, contempt, threatening, delight, triumph, etc., according to the manner of utterance.
ahab: according to the Old Testament he was a pagan king of Israel and husband of Jezebel (th century BC)
aheight: Aloft; on high. Look up aheight.
ahem: An exclamation to call one's attention; hem.
ahimsa: a Buddhist and Hindu and especially Jainist doctrine holding that all forms of life are sacred and urging the avoidance of violence
ahistorical: unconcerned with or unrelated to history or to historical development or to tradition
aho: Initialism of approved hunting organisation, an organisation of which membership is one of several possible prerequisites for a firearms license.
ahold: Near the wind; as, to lay a ship ahold.
ahorseback: On horseback. Two suspicious fellows ahorseback. Smollet.
ahoy: A term used in hailing; as, Ship ahoy. "
ahriman: The Evil Principle or Being of the ancient Persians; the Prince of Darkness as opposer to Ormuzd, the King of Light.
ai: The three-toed sloth (Bradypus tridactyl us) of South America. See Sloth.
aider: One who, or that which, aids.
aiding: present participle and gerund of aid
aidman: An army medical corpsman attached to a field unit.
aids: a serious (often fatal) disease of the immune system transmitted through blood products especially by sexual contact or contaminated needles
aigret: a long plume, especially one of egret feathers, worn on a hat, or a piece of jewelry in the shape of a plume
aigrette: a long plume (especially one of egret feathers) worn on a hat or a piece of jewelry in the shape of a plume
aiguillette: A point or tag at the end of a fringe or lace; an aglet.
aikido: a Japanese martial art employing principles similar to judo
ail: To affect with pain or uneasiness, either physical or mental; to trouble; to be the matter with; used to express some uneasiness or affection, whose cause is unknown; as, what ails the man I known ot what ails him. What aile th thee, Hagar Gen. xxi.
ailantus: A genus of beautiful trees, natives of the East Indies. The tree imperfectly di
aileron: A half gable, as at the end of a penthouse or of the aisle of achurch.
ailing: somewhat ill or prone to illness
ailment: Indisposition; morbid affection of the body; not applied ordinarily to acute diseases. Little ailments. " Landsdowne.
ailurophilia: A fondness or love for cats or other felines.
ailurophobe: A person with an irrational fear or hatred of felines.
aim: To direct or point, as a weapon, at a particular object; to direct, as a missile, an act, or a proceeding, at, to, or against an object; as, to aim a musket or an arrow, the fist or a blow (at something); to aim a satire or a reflection (at some person or vice).
aimara: A South American freshwater river fish, Hoplias aimara.
aimed: simple past and past participle of aim
aimer: One who aims, directs, or points.
aiming: present participle and gerund of aim
aimless: Without aim or purpose; as, an aimless life. Aimlessly, adv. Aimlessness, n.
aimlessly: without aim; in an aimless manner
ain: belonging to or on behalf of a specified person, especially oneself; Scottish variant of own
ainu: A member of an ethnic group on the northern Japanese island of Hokkaido.
air: An artificial or affected manner; show of pride or vanity; haughtiness; as, it is said of a person, he puts on airs. Thackeray.
airbag: A protective system in automobiles in which when a crash occurs, a bag containing nitrogen, formed by the explosive decomposition of sodium azide, quickly inflates in front of the driver or passenger, preventing injury to the head. Side air bags, including the back seat passengers, also prevent injury.
airbill: A waybill for cargo being shipped by air.
airboat: A flat-bottomed boat driven by an in-air propeller and used in shallow water.
airborne: moved or conveyed by or through air
airbus: a subsonic jet airliner operated over short distances
aircheck: A demonstration recording, often intended to show off the talent of an announcer to a prospective employer.
aircoach: An airliner offering relatively cheap but cramped passenger flights.
aircraftman: a noncommissioned officer in the British Royal Air Force
aircraftsman: a noncommissioned officer in the British Royal Air Force
airdate: The date on which a television or radio program is broadcast.
airdrome: an airfield equipped with control tower and hangars as well as accommodations for passengers and cargo
airdrop: delivery of supplies or equipment or personnel by dropping them by parachute from an aircraft
aire: a river in northern England that flows southeast through West Yorkshire
aired: open to or abounding in fresh air
airedale: breed of large wiry-coated terrier bred in Yorkshire
airer: One who exposes to the air.
airfare: the fare charged for traveling by airplane
airfield: a place where planes take off and land
airfoil: a device that provides reactive force when in motion relative to the surrounding air; can lift or control a plane in flight
airforce: the airborne branch of a country's armed forces
airframe: the framework and covering of an airplane or rocket (excluding the engines)
airglow: A faint illumination in the sky due to photochemical luminescence in the upper atmosphere, now rarely observed by earthbound humans without the assistance of instruments.
airiness: the property of something spacious and abounding in fresh air
airing: a short excursion (a walk or ride) in the open air
airless: Not open to a free current of air; wanting fresh air, or communication with the open air.
airlift: fly people or goods to or from places not accessible by other means
airline: a hose that carries air under pressure
airliner: a commercial airplane that carries passengers
airlock: a chamber that provides access to space where air is under pressure
airman: A man who ascends or flies in an aircraft; a flying machine pilot.
airmass: a widespread body of air, the properties of which can be identified as: (a) having been established while that air was situated over a particular region of the Earth's surface (airmass source region) and (b) undergoing specific modifications while in transit away from the source region. An air mass is often defined as a widespread body of air that is approximately homogeneous in its horizontal extent, particularly with reference to temperature and moisture distribution; in addition, the vertical temperature and moisture variations are approximately the same over its horizontal extent.
airpark: A small airport sometimes found near an industrial or business area.
airplane: an aircraft that has a fixed wing and is powered by propellers or jets
airplay: The playing of a particular song, band or genre on the radio, or the frequency with which it is played.
airport: an airfield equipped with control tower and hangars as well as accommodations for passengers and cargo
airpost: a system of conveying mail by aircraft
airs: affected manners intended to impress others
airscape: The view of the sky, or an artistic work that visually represents it.
airscrew: a propeller that rotates to push against air
airsickness: motion sickness experienced while traveling by air (especially during turbulence)
airspace: the space in the atmosphere immediately above the earth
airspeed: the speed of an aircraft relative to the air in which it is flying
airstrip: an airfield without normal airport facilities
airt: to channel into a new direction
airtime: The duration during which a radio or television program (or part of one) is transmitted.
airway: a commercial enterprise that provides scheduled flights for passengers
airwoman: A woman who ascends or flies in an aircraft.
aisle: a long narrow passage (as in a cave or woods)
aistopod: A snake-like amphibian from the order Aistopoda.
ait: An islet, or little isle, in a river or lake; an eyot. The ait where the osiers grew. R. Hod ges.Among green aits and meadows. Dickens.
aitchbone: The bone of the rump; also, the cut of beef surrounding this bone.
aizoaceae: succulent herbs or small shrubs mostly of South Africa but also New Zealand and North America: carpe tweeds; fig marigolds
ajar: Slightly turned or opened; as, the door was standing ajar.
ajax: a mythical Greek hero; a warrior who fought against Troy in the Iliad
ajutage: A tube through which is water is discharged; an efflux tube; as, the ajutage of a fountain.
akan: a Kwa language spoken in Ghana and the Ivory Coast
akaroa: A town on Akaroa Harbour, Banks Peninsula, Canterbury, New Zealand.
akasa: ether or atmosphere, as one of the elements in Hindu philosophy
akazga: The plant Strychnos icaja, traditionally used as an ordeal poison in West Africa.
akebia: Any plant of the genus Akebia, especially the invasive plant Akebia quinata.
akee: widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions for its fragrant flowers and colorful fruits; introduced in Jamaica by William Bligh
akela: A fictional wolf character in Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book.
akepiro: A small tree of New Zealand (Olearia furfuracea).
akhund: A spiritual leader in Persia, parts of Central Asia and Xinjiang, China.
akimbo: With a crook or bend; with the hand on the hip and elbow turned outward. With one arm akimbo. " Irving.
akinesia: Paralysis of the motor nerves; loss of movement. Foster.
aking: present participle and gerund of ake
akkad: One of the ancient kingdoms of Mesopotamia, located in northern Babylonia.
akkadian: an ancient branch of the Semitic languages
aknow: Earlier form of Acknow. To be aknow, to acknowledge; to confess.
akvavit: Scandinavian liquor usually flavored with caraway seeds
alabama: a state in the southeastern United States on the Gulf of Mexico; one of the Confederate states during the American Civil War
alabamian: Pertaining to the American state Alabama, or its natives and residents.
alabandite: A mineral form of manganese sulfide, MnS, sometimes found in meteorites
alabastrine: Of, pertaining to, or like, alabaster; as alabastrine limbs.
alabastron: A kind of ancient pottery vase used for holding oils, and originally made from alabaster.
alacrious: Brisk; joyously active; lively.'T were well if we were a little more alacrious. Hammond.
alacrity: A cheerful readiness, willingness, or promptitude; joyous activity; briskness; sprightliness; as, the soldiers advanced with alacrity to meet the enemy. I have not that alacrity of spirit, Nor cheer of mind that I was wont to have.
alameda: A tree-lined avenue in Spain or Portugal.
alamo: a siege and massacre at a mission in San Antonio in; Mexican forces under Santa Anna besieged and massacred American rebels who were fighting to make Texas independent of Mexico
alamode: According to the fashion or prevailing mode. Alamode beef shops. " Macaulay.
aland: On land; to the land; ashore. Cast aland. " Sir P. Sidney.
alanine: A white crystalline base, CHNO, derived from aldehyde ammonia.
alans: clothing worn under other clothing, underwear
alantolactone: The sesquiterpene lactone aR,S,aR,aR-a,,,a,a-octahydro-,a-dimethylmethylene-naphtho[,-b]furan-(H)-one which inhibits proliferation of cancer cells
alap: The opening, improvised section of a Classical raga performance, before the formal recitation.
alar: Axillary; in the fork or axil. Gray.
alarm: fear resulting from the awareness of danger

alarming: Exciting, or calculated to excite, alarm; causing apprehension of danger; as, an alarming crisis or report. Alarmingly, adv.
alarmist: One prone to sound or excite alarms, especially, needless alarms. Macaulay.
alary: Of or pertaining to wings; also, wing-shaped. The alary system of insects. Wollaston.
alas: An exclamation expressive of sorrow, pity, or apprehension of evil; in old writers, sometimes followed by day or white; alas the day, like alack a day, or alas the white.
alaska: a state in northwestern North America; the th state admitted to the union
alaskan: relating to or characteristic of the state or people of Alaska

alate: Lately; of late. There hath been alate such tales spread abroad. Latimer.

albert: prince consort of Queen Victoria of England (-)
alberta: one of the three prairie provinces in western Canada; rich in oil and natural gas and minerals
albertype: A picture printed from a kind of gelatine plate produced by means of a photographic negative.
albi: A town and commune, the prefecture of Tarn department, Occitania, in southern France.

albigenses: a Christian religious sect in southern France in the th and th centuries; believers in Albigensianism
albigensian: Of or pertaining to the Albigenses.

albin: A male given name from Latin.
albinism: The state or condition of being an albino: abinoism; leucopathy.

albion: An ancient name of England, still retained in poetry. In that nook-shotten isle of Albion.

albizzia: any of numerous trees of the genus Albizia

albuminise: Non-Oxford British English spelling of albuminize.
albuminosis: A morbid condition due to excessive increase of albuminous elements in the blood.
albuminous: relating to or containing or resembling albumin
albuminuria: A morbid condition in which albumin is present in the urine.
albumose: A compound or class of compounds formed from albumin by dilute acids or by an acid solution of pepsin. Used also in combination, as antialbumose, hemialbumose.
alburn: The bleak, a small European fish having scales of a peculiarly silvery color which are used in making artificial pearls.
alburnous: Of or pertaining to alburnum; of the alburnum; as, alburnous substances.
alburnum: The white and softer part of wood, between the inner bark and the hard wood or duramen; sapwood.
albyn: Scotland; esp. the Highlands of Scotland. T. Cam bell.
alca: type genus of the Alcidae comprising solely the razorbill
alcaide: The governor or commander of a Spanish or Portuguese fortress or prison.
alcalde: A magistrate or judge in Spain and in Spanish America, etc. Prescott.
alcazar: A fortress; also, a royal palace. Prescott.
alcedo: A genus of perching birds, including the European kingfisher (Alcedo ispida). See Halcyon.
alchemic: related to or concerned with alchemy
alchemical: related to or concerned with alchemy
alchemilla: Any of the genus Alchemilla of herbaceous perennial plants.
alchemist: One who practices alchemy. You are alchemist; make gold.
alchemize: To change by alchemy; to transmute. Lovelace.
alcibiades: ancient Athenian statesman and general in the Peloponnesian War (circa - BC)
alcid: A bird of the family Alcidae, including auks, auklets, razorbills, dovekies, guillemots, and puffins.
alcidae: web-footed diving seabirds of northern seas: auks; puffins; guillemots; murres; etc.
alcohol: A class of compounds analogous to vinic alcohol in constitution. alcoholate: A crystallizable compound of a salt with alcohol, in which the latter plays a part analogous to that of water of crystallization. Graham.
alcoholic: Of or pertaining to alcohol, or partaking of its qualities; derived from, or caused by, alcohol; containing alcohol; as, alcoholic mixtures; alcoholic gastritis; alcoholic odor.
alcoholise: to make alcoholic, as by fermenting
alcoholism: A diseased condition of the system, brought about by the continued use of alcoholic liquors.
alcoholization: The act of reducing a substance to a fine or impalpable powder. Johnson.
alcoholize: An instrument for determining the strength of spirits, with ascale graduated so as to indicate the percentage of pure alcohol, either by weight or volume. It is usually a form of hydrometer with aspecial scale.
alcoholized: simple past and past participle of alcoholize
alcoholometer: A specialized form of hydrometer used to measure the amount of alcohol in a liquid (such as beer).
alcoholometric: Of or pertaining to the measurement of the alcohol content of beers, wines and spirits
alcoran: The Mohammedan Scriptures; the Koran (now the usual form).
alcoranic: Of or pertaining to the Koran.

alcornoque: The bark of several trees, esp. of Bowdichia virgilioides of brazil, used as a remedy for consumption; of Byrsonima crassifolia, used in tanning; of Alchornea latifolia, used medicinally; or of quercus ilex, the cork tree.
alcove: A recessed portion of a room, or a small room opening into alar ger one; especially, a recess to contain a bed; a lateral recess in a library.

alcyone: (Greek mythology) a woman who was turned into a kingfisher
alcyonium: A genus of fleshy Alcyonaria, its polyps somewhat resembling flowers with eight fringed rays. The term was also formerly used for certain species of sponges.
alcyonoid: Like or pertaining to the Alcyonaria. n.
aldebaran: A red star of the first magnitude, situated in the eye of taurus; the Bull's Eye. It is the bright star in the group called the hyades. Now when Aldebaran was mounted high Above the shiny Cassiopeia'sc hair. Spenser.
aldehyde: A colorless, mobile, and very volatile liquid obtained from alcohol by certain of oxidation.
aldehydic: Of or pertaining to aldehyde; as, aldehydic acid. Miller.
alder: A tree, usually growing in moist land, and belonging to the genus Alnus. The wood is used by turners, etc.; the bark by dyers and tanners. In the U. S. the species of alder are usually shrubs or small trees. Black alder. (a) A European shrub (Rhamnus frangula);Alder buckthorn. (b) An American species of holly (Ilexverticillata), bearing red berries.
alderfly: dark-colored insect having predaceous aquatic larvae
alderman: a member of a municipal legislative body (as a city council)
aldermanic: Relating to, becoming to, or like, an alderman; characteristic of an alderman.
aldermanry: The district or ward of an alderman.

alditol: Any of a class of acyclic polyols formally derived from an aldose by reduction of the carbonyl functional group.
aldohexose: a monosaccharide sugar having six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group
aldol: A colorless liquid, CHO, obtained by condensation of two molecules of acetaldehyde: CHCHO + CHCHO = HCH (OH) CHCO; also, anyof various derivatives of this. The same reaction has been applied, under the name of aldol condensation, to the production of many compounds.

aldoxime: Any oxime derived from an aldehyde; general formula RCH=NOH
aldrin: An insecticide and persistent organic pollutant containing a naphthalene-derived compound.

aleatory: Depending on some uncertain contingency; as, an aleatory contract. Bouvier.

alecithal: Applied to those ova which segment uniformly, and which have little or no food yelk embedded in their protoplasm. Balfour.

alecost: The plant costmary, which was formerly much used for flavoring ale.
alectoria: lichens having dark brown erect or pendulous much-branched cylindrical thallus
